title: Latent Diffusion-based Data Augmentation for Continuous-Time Dynamic Graph Model

problem.claim: Continuous-Time Dynamic Graph models face noise and limited historical data.

gap.claim: Existing graph data augmentation methods primarily target static graphs, struggle with CTDG dynamics, require substantial domain expertise for parameter tuning, and lack theoretical guarantees for augmentation efficacy.

contributions.claim: Conda is a latent diffusion-based graph data augmentation method tailored for CTDGs.
Conda combines a Variational Auto-Encoder and a conditional diffusion model to generate enhanced historical neighbor embeddings for target nodes.
The method uses target-node historical neighbor sequence embeddings for training and an alternating training strategy when integrated with a CTDG model.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Conda as a novel latent diffusion-based graph data augmentation method tailored for CTDGs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments across six widely used real-world datasets reportedly show consistent performance improvement, especially with limited historical data.

narrative_sequence.summary: CTDGs model evolving real-world relationships and are important in dynamic graph learning.
Existing CTDG models and augmentation methods face noise, limited historical data, dynamic-graph mismatch, tuning demands, and missing theoretical guarantees.
Conda applies a VAE and conditional diffusion model to generate enhanced historical neighbor embeddings for target nodes.
Conda trains on target-node historical neighbor sequence embeddings and uses alternating training within a CTDG model.
The authors report consistent improvement across six real-world datasets, particularly under limited historical data.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the CTDG tasks, baselines, metrics, or dataset identities.
The abstract does not provide quantitative effect sizes or ablation results.
The abstract does not describe theoretical guarantees or explain how parameter-tuning demands are reduced.
